findings.section: Cache headers decide how long a copy lives and versioned names replace it sooner (Exam trap)
findings.quote: and daily invalidations soon use up the free paths
findings.type: claims: unsupported claim, contradicted by the chapter's own facts
findings.evidence: No fact supports it, and two verified facts refute it. cloudfront-invalidation-first-1000-paths-free: "The first 1,000 invalidation paths that you submit per month are free; you pay for each invalidation path over 1,000 in a month." cloudfront-invalidation-wildcard-counts-one-path: "A path that includes the `*` wildcard counts as one path even if it causes CloudFront to invalidate thousands of files." One invalidation a day is about 30 paths a month (one with a wildcard), far below 1,000. The chapter's own spoken answer cloudfront-s03 says the opposite: "The thing to watch is the real reason. It isn't mainly cost." Fix: drop the clause, or give the real reason from cloudfront-invalidation-prefer-versioning-for-frequent-updates (versioning also controls copies in browsers and corporate proxies; invalidation does not).
findings.resolution: fix-15: the clause is gone. The trap now gives the real reason: a new name also replaces copies in browsers and proxies, which an invalidation does not clear. The A-list cell 'Frequent releases pay' is now 'A wildcard path counts as one'. Speak cloudfront-s03 aligned (claims-16).

findings.section: Decision record (after figure, step 4); also diagrams/src/cloudfront-after.json edge 4 say text
findings.quote: 4. Dynamic requests go to the load balancer, whose security group allows the CloudFront prefix list.
findings.type: technical: insecure recommendation that contradicts the chapter's own best practice
findings.evidence: The prefix list admits every CloudFront distribution, not only Callvale's. full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide (Use the CloudFront managed prefix list): "This allows all of the CloudFront global origin-facing servers to reach the instance." For an internet-facing ALB, AWS lists the mitigation (full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide, Restrict access to Application Load Balancers): "Configure CloudFront to add a custom HTTP header to requests that it sends to the Application Load Balancer." and "Configure the Application Load Balancer to only forward requests that contain the custom HTTP header." The chapter itself teaches both locks: the origin-lock ladder says "Prefix list and header", and shipped question cloudfront-q012 keys prefix list PLUS secret header for "only requests that come through the company's own distribution". The chapter also calls VPC origins "the newest and recommended solution" (cloudfront-dec-ddos-wp-vpc-origins-newest-recommended). Fix: make the decision a VPC origin (internal ALB), or the prefix list plus a custom header and a listener rule; update the figure's step 4 text to match.
findings.resolution: fix-15: decision step 4 and the cloudfront-after spec say now read 'Dynamic requests go to the load balancer, locked by the prefix list and a secret header.' (SVG rebuilt). The trade-off says the load balancer stays internet-facing and a VPC origin can come later. The VPC origins subsection now teaches both locks with elb-alb-cloudfront-prefix-list-sg, cloudfront-alb-restrict-custom-header-and-https and cloudfront-prefix-list-origin-facing-servers (all CloudFront servers pass the prefix list).

findings.section: CloudFront encrypts two separate connections and each one has its own setting (Spot the bug answer)
findings.quote: The ALB can keep its own: [import the certificate in any AWS Region](../facts/acm.md#acm-cloudfront-origin-certificate-any-region).
findings.type: technical: misleading; the link is right but the sentence reads as if an ALB can use a certificate from any Region
findings.evidence: The fact's quote means the origin certificate is not tied to us-east-1, not that a load balancer can use a certificate from another Region. full:acm-userguide (Supported Regions): "Certificates in ACM are regional resources. To use a certificate with Elastic Load Balancing for the same fully qualified domain name (FQDN) or set of FQDNs in more than one AWS region, you must request or import a certificate for each region." ... "You cannot copy a certificate between regions." The chapter's own question cloudfront-q014 rejects "Request both certificates in US East (N. Virginia)" with acm-certificates-regional. Placed in an eu-west-1 scenario, "in any AWS Region" invites exactly the wrong belief that q014 tests. Fix: say the ALB keeps its certificate from its own Region (eu-west-1), linking acm-faq-certificate-same-region-as-resource.
findings.resolution: fix-15: first rewritten with acm-faq-certificate-same-region-as-resource, then the whole TLS Spot the bug was removed to bring 2-deep.md under its 4,500-word limit (L201). The misleading sentence is gone; step 2 keeps the US East (N. Virginia) rule for the CloudFront certificate, and q014 still tests the ALB Region. The cache behaviors Spot the bug keeps the spot_the_bug count at 1.

findings.section: In one breath (picture steps 3 and 4); also 2-deep.md How it works step 4 and diagrams/src/cloudfront-hero.json claim and aside
findings.quote: 3. On a miss, the request goes to the regional edge cache, which has [a larger cache](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-rec-larger-cache-than-pop).
findings.type: claims: oversimplified, stated as always true; verified exceptions left out
findings.evidence: full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide (How CloudFront works with regional edge caches): "Proxy HTTP methods (`PUT`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `OPTIONS`, and `DELETE`) go directly to the origin from the POPs and do not proxy through the regional edge caches." "Dynamic requests, as determined at request time, do not flow through regional edge caches, but go directly to the origin." "When the origin is an Amazon S3 bucket and the request's optimal regional edge cache is in the same AWS Region as the S3 bucket, the POP skips the regional edge cache and goes directly to the S3 bucket." Verified facts exist and are unused: cloudfront-rec-proxy-methods-skip, cloudfront-rec-dynamic-requests-skip, cloudfront-rec-skipped-same-region-s3. The same claim is in 2-deep.md ("Climb on a miss. The next stop is a regional edge cache.") and the hero aside "Both caches keep a copy". It matters for Callvale: its buckets are in US East (N. Virginia). Fix: say "typically" and add the three exceptions in a Go deeper block.
findings.resolution: fix-15: 'typically' added to 2-deep step 4 and to hero step 3 (1-fast.md and cloudfront-hero spec say, SVG rebuilt). New Go deeper block in 2-deep: dynamic requests (cloudfront-rec-dynamic-requests-skip) and S3 origins in the same Region (cloudfront-rec-skipped-same-region-s3) go straight to the origin. The hero aside shows the drawn GET case and stays.

findings.section: CloudFront encrypts two separate connections and each one has its own setting
findings.quote: Why two settings? CloudFront [terminates TLS close to viewers](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-pricing-page-dynamic-acceleration-mechanisms) and opens a new TLS connection to the origin.
findings.type: claims: the link supports only the first half; the sentence says more
findings.evidence: cloudfront-pricing-page-dynamic-acceleration-mechanisms quotes: "CloudFront terminates TLS close to viewers from distributed edge locations, maintains persistent connections to your origin, ..." Nothing says it opens a new TLS connection, and with the origin protocol policy HTTP (row 1 of the table directly above) there is no TLS to the origin at all. Fix: "... and opens a separate connection to the origin, HTTP or HTTPS by the origin protocol policy", or link cloudfront-https-viewer-origin-protocol-independent.
findings.resolution: fix-15: now 'CloudFront terminates TLS close to viewers and opens a separate connection to the origin, with the protocol that the origin protocol policy sets.' No claim of a second TLS connection.

findings.section: An origin group fails over to a second origin when the first one fails (Stop and answer); also Numbers A-list row and card cloudfront-c019
findings.quote: by default CloudFront can wait as long as [30 seconds](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-default-connect-wait-before-failover) before the secondary.
findings.type: technical: condition dropped from the fact (connection attempts only)
findings.evidence: The 30 seconds are 3 connection attempts of 10 seconds: "By default, CloudFront waits as long as 30 seconds (3 attempts of 10 seconds each) before attempting to connect to the secondary origin or returning an error response." (full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide, Connection attempts). An origin that accepts the connection but does not answer is governed by the response timeout: "For response timeout, the default is 30 seconds." and for GET and HEAD "CloudFront drops the connection. CloudFront tries again to connect according to the value of Connection attempts." So in an outage the wait can be longer than 30 seconds. Card cloudfront-c019 makes it an upper bound ("waits up to 30 seconds"). Fix: say "when the primary refuses connections" and mention the response timeout.
findings.resolution: fix-15: Stop-and-answer now says connection attempts to an unreachable primary take 30 seconds by default and a primary that connects but does not answer adds a response timeout. A-list label: 'CloudFront connection attempts before the secondary origin'. Card cloudfront-c019 front names connection attempts; its extra adds the response timeout with cloudfront-default-response-timeout.

findings.section: VPC origins let CloudFront reach load balancers and instances in private subnets (step 3 and Say it)
findings.quote: 3. **Keep a gateway.** [You need to add an internet gateway](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-vpc-origin-needs-internet-gateway) to the VPC.
findings.type: technical: condition dropped from the fact; can push the reader to make the subnet public
findings.evidence: cloudfront-vpc-origin-needs-internet-gateway quotes: "The internet gateway is required to denote that the VPC can receive traffic from the internet. The internet gateway is not used for routing traffic to origins inside the subnet, and you don't need to update the routing policies." The chapter keeps only the first sentence, and the Say it line ("The thing to watch is the internet gateway.") adds weight. A reader who adds a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the gateway makes the subnet public, which defeats the VPC origin. Fix: add "no route to it is needed; the subnet stays private" with the second display of the same fact.
findings.resolution: fix-15: step 3 now reads '... to the VPC, but it does not route traffic to the subnet. The subnet stays private.' in the sentence linked to cloudfront-vpc-origin-needs-internet-gateway (the second link was dropped for the word limit).

findings.section: Health checks and traffic dials move new connections from one Region to another (table)

findings.evidence: global-accelerator-failover-to-another-endpoint-group-ignores-dial: "If there are no healthy endpoints in an endpoint group that have a weight greater than zero, Global Accelerator tries to fail over to a healthy endpoint with a weight greater than zero in another endpoint group. Note that for this failover, Global Accelerator ignores the traffic dial setting." findings.section: Changed recently (whole section; the OAC entry was removed at edit)
findings.quote: > **Changed recently:** (2024-11-20) VPC origins for private subnets.
findings.type: rule: RULINGS hard rule 7 (Changed recently for a fact changed since mid-2022)
findings.evidence: OAC replaced OAI as the recommended way after mid-2022. full:amazoncloudfront-developerguide (Document history): "... with origin access control](#private-content-restricting-access-to-s3) | You can now secure Amazon S3 origins by permitting access to only the designated CloudFront distributions. | August 24, 2022 |". RULINGS rule 7: "Where a fact changed since mid-2022, add a 'Changed recently' note with old value, new value, date, and what older exam questions may assume." The ledger note of edit-15 says "OAC 2022 Changed recently entry removed"; the trap line ("Older practice questions still name OAI") gives no date and no old/new pair. findings.resolution: fix-15: cannot be grounded in this stage. L107 requires the date to equal changed.date of a verified fact linked in Now:, and the canon has no verified OAC launch fact. findings.section: cloudfront-t03 verify
findings.quote: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --region us-west-2 --tag-filters Key=task,Values=cloudfront-t03 --query "ResourceTagMappingList[].ResourceARN"
findings.type: technical: verify step that may not be able to fail
findings.evidence: The expected result is "An empty list". No saved page shows that the Resource Groups Tagging API returns Global Accelerator accelerators; the Global Accelerator tagging page (full:global-accelerator-dg, Tagging in AWS Global Accelerator) names only "the AWS console, AWS CLI, or Global Accelerator API" and "AWS Global Accelerator supports tagging for accelerators and cross-account attachments."
